overview: Matrix algebra ke basic ideas: determinant, rank, inverse, singular/non-singular, symmetric counting, trace, null space, orthogonal/projection matrices, LU factorization.
whyItMatters: 24 PYQs, 1987-2026; recent saalon me MSQ 'always correct' statements common hain.
coreConcept: Square matrix A invertible <=> det(A) != 0 <=> full rank <=> rows/columns linearly independent <=> Ax=0 ka sirf trivial solution.
hinglishExplanation: Matrix ke bahut saare properties ek hi baat ke different chehre hain: singular = determinant 0 = rows dependent = null space non-trivial. Isliye statement check karte waqt in equivalences ko use karo. Counting questions me free entries gino: n x n symmetric 0/1 matrix ke liye 2^(n(n+1)/2).
formalDefinition: rank(A) = number of linearly independent rows = dimension of column space.
importantProperties: det(AB) = det(A)det(B); det(A^T) = det(A); det(kA) = k^n det(A); det(A^-1) = 1/det(A).
Row swap det ka sign badalta hai; row addition det nahi badalti; scaling det ko scale karti hai.
rank(A) + nullity(A) = number of columns (rank-nullity theorem).
trace(AB) = trace(BA); trace = sum of diagonal = sum of eigenvalues.
Symmetric n x n matrices with 0/1 entries: 2^(n(n+1)/2).
Orthogonal matrix: Q^T Q = I, norm-preserving, det = +/-1.
Sum of two singular matrices non-singular ho sakti hai aur two non-singular ka sum singular ho sakta hai.
AB = I (square) => BA = I, dono inverse hain.
keyPropertiesAndIdentities: Elementary row operations rank preserve karte hain.
Nilpotent/idempotent conditions se invertibility decide karo.
commonPitfalls: det(A+B) = det A + det B maan lena (galat).
det(kA) = k det A (n dimension ka power bhoolna).
AB = BA maan lena (matrices generally commute nahi karte).
Null space vector ke saath det ke conclusion.
standardTechniques: Statement 'ALWAYS true' me chhota counter-example try karo.
